facts.text: Curated gallery of artisans and fine artists from Northwest Philadelphia, run by the Roxborough Development Corporation.
Began as a temporary pop-up and is now a permanent fixture on Ridge Avenue.
Multidisciplinary arts center in Chinatown North with exhibitions, performances and artist residencies.
Occupies a multi-tenant building from 1906 that was once a film storage house and medical supply depot.
Gallery established in 2011, showing pop, abstract, neo-street and contemporary art.
Shows emerging and mid-career artists working in all mediums.
Ship was built at the Philadelphia Naval Shipyard and commissioned into the Navy on May 23, 1943.
Ship was laid down in September 1940 and launched on December 7, 1942.
Underground museum with artifacts, videos and computer interactives about Franklin's life.
Exhibits are organized around five Franklin traits, including curious and strategic.
Studio and gallery of ceramic sculptor Michael Biello and composer Dan Martin.
Biello has kept an atelier in Old City Philadelphia since 1996.
Housed in a historic 1890s steam plant in Fishtown.
Has two spaces with vintage chandeliers, exposed brick walls and cobblestone areas.
Gallery established in 2001 by Bridgette Mayer, showing contemporary painting, sculpture and photography.
Reopened to the public at its Washington Square location in June 2021.
Art museum for Alexander Calder's work, designed by Herzog & de Meuron on a 1.8-acre site.
Gardens by Piet Oudolf hold over 250 varieties of plants around the building.
Run by the Northeast Regional Council of Carpenters and holds artifacts from the 1881 founding of the carpenters union.
Displays Peter J. McGuire's union membership cards and rare 1875 Pike and Dean planes.
Art studio focused on the professional development of artists with intellectual disabilities.
Studio programs include ceramics, painting, sculpture, printmaking, woodshop, fiber arts and music.
Former Municipal Pier 9, a 65,000 square foot shipping pier on the Delaware River waterfront.
Artists work in repurposed shipping containers that give the public access to their process.
COSACOSA art at large is a non-profit creating public art with Philadelphia neighborhood residents.
Its projects have brought Philadelphians together since 1990.
Museum occupies houses 124 and 126 and is run by the Elfreth's Alley Association.
The alley dates to 1703 and has houses built between 1720 and 1836.
Housed in the former Engine Company 8 firehouse, occupied by the company in 1899.
Tells the history of firefighting in Philadelphia through artifacts and archives.
Founded by Tyler School of Art graduates in a North Philadelphia warehouse.
Combines artist studios, communal work space and exhibition space.
Exhibit in the Franklin Court courtyard, beside the Benjamin Franklin Museum.
Franklin Court was first excavated by archeologists in 1953.
Gallery founded in 1969 by Estelle Shane Gross.
Moved to 16th Street in 1986, into a renovated old hotel.
Neoclassical house at The Woodlands, former country seat of William Hamilton.
In 1840 the estate's core was bought to become a rural cemetery.
Exhibition and event space for high-end glass artworks by the local Illadelph art collective.
The collective has produced glass art since 2002.
Heather Karlie Fine Art opened 20th Century by HKFA at this address in May 2012.
Heather Karlie Fine Art started the Fishtown Pop Up gallery at this address with a New York artist's show.
Gallery operating since 1988, showing abstract and conceptual art with an emphasis on painting.
Represents emerging, mid-career and internationally recognized artists, many from Philadelphia.
Opened in 1976 as part of Philadelphia's Bicentennial celebration.
Exhibits costumes, oral histories, video and audio archives, and a strutting lesson.

name: St. George's United Methodist Church House Museum and Library

facts.text: Known as the Cradle of American Methodism and the world's oldest Methodist church in continuous service.
A historical center and museum adjoin the church.
Specializes in 20th century contemporary prints, paintings and sculpture.
Located in Rittenhouse Square since 1995.
